name: date-picker
title: Date picker
description: A date field with a calendar popover, Today and Clear actions, markers and unavailable days.

when: Picking a date where seeing the month helps.

instead.when: A start and an end are picked together.

builtIn: Required fields show "Fill in this field."; a partly typed date says what is missing.

genui.description: A date field with a calendar. Emits change.

label.description: Always given; the label sits above the field and names its segments.

granularity.description:
`month`: a year and a month, for a report or history range. The field types month and year
(as DateField `granularity="month"`), the value is that month's first day, and the popover is a grid of the
twelve months under a year stepper, with "This month" and "Clear"; `minValue` and `maxValue` count by month.
The day-only props (unavailable days, markers, first day of the week) do not apply. Default `day`.

DatePicker.name: id
DatePicker.description:
The id of the field's first typed segment (day, or the locale's first part), the element that takes focus
: `document.getElementById(id).focus()` puts the user in the field, as a focus-on-error does. The
field's group gets an id of its own. Left out, the DOM is as before.

DatePicker.name: name
DatePicker.description: The form field name; the value is submitted as an ISO string.

DatePicker.name: label
DatePicker.description: Always given; the label sits above the field and names its segments.

DatePicker.name: errorMessage
DatePicker.description: What happened and what to do; shown when the field is invalid.

DatePicker.name: requiredValidation
DatePicker.description:
Who says an empty required field is missing: `field` (default) or `app`. With `app` a DS
Form's `onSubmit` runs with the field empty, and the app's own error must clear on change. See
{@link RequiredValidation} for the whole contract.

DatePicker.name: isOptional
DatePicker.description: Shows "(optional)" when most of the form is required.

DatePicker.name: isInvalid
DatePicker.description: Marks the field invalid from outside (a server error); `errorMessage` says why.

DatePicker.name: validate
DatePicker.type: (value: CalendarDate | null) => string | true | string[] | null | undefined
DatePicker.description: Your own check; return the message to show, or nothing when the date is fine.

DatePicker.name: value
DatePicker.description:
A calendar date, no time zone; with `granularity="month"` the month's first day.

While the user leaves a date typed in part or impossible ("31.aa.2026", "31.11.2026"), the field reports
`onChange(null)` and keeps the typed parts on screen, so setting `null` changes nothing: the value already is null.
To clear the field (an app's own "Temizle" or form reset), give it a new `key` along with the value: React remounts
it empty, or at the value given.

DatePicker.name: timeZone
DatePicker.description: "Today" in the calendar and the Today action: the location's zone; the device's by default.

DatePicker.name: shouldCloseOnSelect
DatePicker.description: Close the calendar once a day is picked (default).

DatePicker.name: granularity
DatePicker.description:
`month`: a year and a month, for a report or history range. The field types month and year
(as DateField `granularity="month"`), the value is that month's first day, and the popover is a grid of the
twelve months under a year stepper, with "This month" and "Clear"; `minValue` and `maxValue` count by month.
The day-only props (unavailable days, markers, first day of the week) do not apply. Default `day`.
